Change c0358. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. II; 1831 Ch. XIX.

Context before (unchanged): This city had remained faithful to him, after the whole nation had forsaken his cause to join the standard of parliament and liberty.

1818 text: The memory of that unfortunate king, and his companions, the amiable Falkland, the insolent Gower, his queen, and son, gave a peculiar interest to every part of the city, which they might be supposed to have inhabited.

1831 text: The memory of that unfortunate king, and his companions, the amiable Falkland, the insolent Goring, his queen, and son, gave a peculiar interest to every part of the city, which they might be supposed to have inhabited.

Diff: The memory of that unfortunate king, and his companions, the amiable Falkland, the insolent [-Gower-] {+Goring+} , his queen, and son, gave a peculiar interest to every part of the city, which they might be supposed to have inhabited.

Context after (unchanged): The spirit of elder days found a dwelling here, and we delighted to trace its footsteps.

result.rationale: Gower to Goring corrects a proper name: the courtier George Goring, a historical figure in Charles I's court, replacing the invented Gower. It is a factual/name correction, not a change in wording or meaning of the passage.
